checks.explanation: The claim is a verbatim quote from the source document describing the design of a gearbox housing, setting fits, and using interference checks. The category 'project' is appropriate for this described engineering task.

The student explicitly uses the first-person pronoun 'I' to describe designing a specific component (gearbox housing) and revising an assembly. This establishes individual ownership of the work, supporting the 'led' label which requires explicit individual contribution or independent ownership.

The student describes making specific design choices: setting bearing and shaft fits from stated tolerances and using interference checks to revise the assembly. These actions go beyond simple tool usage or application, demonstrating adaptation to constraints and design decisions, supporting the 'designed' depth label.
The student explicitly mentions using 'interference checks' as a method to assess the assembly fit. This constitutes a concrete test or assessment method, supporting the 'described' evaluation label.

The student reports that they 'revised the assembly' based on the interference checks. Reporting a concrete outcome (the revision of the assembly) supports the 'reported' impact label without requiring external verification or measurement metrics.

The source text describes creating a gearbox housing, setting fits, and revising an assembly using specific geometric constraints (tolerances, interference checks). This aligns with the definition of mechanical_design as creation/refinement of mechanical parts through explicit geometry and fit choices.

The student used 'interference checks' within SolidWorks. Interference checks are a form of physics-based or numerical model execution/interpretation used to study assembly behavior (clearance/fit), supporting the engineering_simulation competency.

The rationale correctly identifies that while parametric modeling involves logic, there is no explicit mention of writing code, scripts, or macros. The source only supports CAD usage and design tasks. Per instructions, tool recognition alone does not establish a demonstrated programming competency, and the absence of explicit 'code writing' verbs means this claim is unsupported.
The student explicitly states they used SolidWorks to perform the design tasks. This correctly identifies the tool used in the context of the project.
The source text mentions setting 'bearing and shaft fits', which are specific mechanical engineering concepts related to tolerancing. Recognizing this concept is allowed within the context.
The source text mentions using 'interference checks', a specific method for evaluating geometric conflicts. Recognizing this concept is allowed within the context.
The source text mentions setting fits 'from the stated tolerances', indicating knowledge and application of tolerance concepts. Recognizing this concept is allowed within the context.

dimensions.description: Individual contribution explicitly described in the evidence.

labels.assisted: Explicitly supported another contributor or followed guided work.
labels.shared: Explicit individual contribution within collaborative work.
labels.led: Explicitly directed the work or independently owned the deliverable; a title or possessive like my thesis alone is insufficient.

dimensions.description: Nature of the work demonstrated by the description, not prestige.

labels.unknown: A title, skill list, or credential alone does not describe the work.
labels.applied: Used established methods to implement or complete a described task.
labels.designed: Made and explained design choices or adapted methods to constraints.
labels.investigated: Investigated a question through an explicit method and analysis.

dimensions.description: How the work was evaluated; no implied ordering across disciplines.

labels.compared: Evaluation includes explicit baselines, alternatives, or controls.
labels.externally_reviewed: External assessment is explicitly stated; this remains a claim until verified.

dimensions.description: Evidence describing results, separate from their independent verification.

labels.reported: A concrete outcome is reported without a measurement method.
labels.measured: An outcome and measurement method or comparison are stated.
labels.adopted: Actual use or adoption by identified users or an organization is stated.

category_guidance.project: Distinguish guided replication from individual design. Tool names do not establish depth. Preserve team contribution and ask about missing evaluation.
category_guidance.work: Assess described responsibilities and contributions. Employer reputation and job title do not establish ownership. Do not sum overlapping durations.
category_guidance.research: Unpublished research can demonstrate investigation. Evaluate methods and contribution independently of publication status; do not invent publications.
category_guidance.publication: Separate paper content, authorship, and review status. Do not rank unfamiliar venues or assume arXiv entails peer review. Request metadata verification later.
category_guidance.coursework: Preserve course and grade context. Enrollment alone does not establish mastery or independent implementation.
category_guidance.education: Preserve every degree and original grade scale separately. No prestige adjustment or invented grade conversion. Do not infer completion from attendance dates.
category_guidance.activity: Assess individual contribution in community, creative, leadership, and school activities without requiring technical work or publications.
category_guidance.other: Preserve unfamiliar evidence and uncertainty. Do not force it into a known technical competency or discard it because of taxonomy coverage.
